subject: Acme launch delay — request for one-time credit / price remediation
messages:
From: Daniel Park <dpark@acme.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Tue, 21 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: commercial remediation for delayed multi-model routing support (Acme)

Tessa,

Quick note from the Acme launch team — thanks again for the support on the integration. We hit a blocker this morning: our production routing strategy requires the multi-model switch we expected in Redwood's upcoming runtime patch. With that missing, our latency is ~2.3x and the UX fails our SLAs for the pilot customers.

We have no good path to go-live next week unless we accept reduced performance. That would mean losing the anchor pilot and delaying our wider rollout to Q3. Given the schedule slip (and the integration work already done), procurement is requesting a one-time commercial remediation — either a temporary rate reduction for the first 3 months post-go-live or a one-off credit to offset the launch impact.

I've attached a short impact spreadsheet for context. Can you route this to the right folks internally? We need a response this week if possible.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Director, Platform Integrations
Acme Corp
attachments: acme_impact_breakdown.xlsx
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <dpark@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Feb 2028 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: commercial remediation for delayed multi-model routing support (Acme)

Daniel — thanks for the clear summary and the spreadsheet. I appreciate the timeline pressure.

Internal note: looping in Rishi (commercial) and Laura (legal/procurement) to evaluate options and next steps. I will also pull product to confirm the delivery horizon and whether there's an engineering mitigation we can ship faster.

Proposed next steps:
- Internal quick sync (today): Rishi / Laura / Product to size the ask and the financial impact.
- Proposal to Acme by EOD Thu 2/23 with option A (credit) and option B (temporary rate reduction + SLAs).

Rishi/Laura — are you available for a short sync at 11:00 PT?

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Feb 2028 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request: commercial remediation for delayed multi-model routing support (Acme)

Forwarding Acme's ask from this morning. TL;DR: their go-live depends on the multi-model routing behavior in the 1.11 runtime; they estimate a material customer and revenue impact if we cannot provide a temporary commercial remedy.

Marcus — can product confirm whether there is a feasible workaround (config change / prefix caching tweak) we can ship in the next 2–3 weeks? If not, we need a commercial recommendation (credit vs. temporary rate) to propose. Rishi / Laura: please advise what level of concession needs leadership sign-off.

Notes for sync at 11:00:
- Impact summary: see attached spreadsheet.
- Desired outcome: proposal with numbers by EOD Thu 2/23.

Thanks — Tessa
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Feb 2028 15:26:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: commercial remediation for delayed multi-model routing support (Acme)

Team — quick product check from the infra side. We cannot fully deliver the multi-model routing feature in the 1.11 patch this month; the remaining blocker is a kernel scheduling contention that needs a deeper regression fix. Realistically the soonest we can ship a stable, opt-in multi-model path is the May 2028 release (we can try a limited internal canary earlier, but not safe for GA). See attached sketch of the timeline delta.

Short-term mitigation options I see:
- Config-level compromise: we can enable coarser routing and aggressive KV-prefetch for Acme's workload within 7–10 days. This will recover 60–75% of the perf gap but not the full SLA.
- Temporary model-variant fallback: route a subset of requests to a lower-cost variant to preserve latency, with quality trade-offs.

Given the above, my recommendation: we pair a short-term engineering mitigation (7–10 days) with a financial concession to share the launch risk. A limited credit or a 3-month stepped rate discount tied to observed token volume seems reasonable. I estimate the credit needed to keep them whole for the pilot is in the $30k–$60k range depending on final volumes.

Attachments: timeline-delta.pdf
Marcus Lin
Director, Product — Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Feb 2028 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: commercial remediation for delayed multi-model routing support (Acme)

Appreciate the rapid triage. Based on Marcus's estimate and our ARR profile with Acme, here's a proposed commercial path: 

Option A (credit): one-time account credit of $50,000 applied to the first invoice after go-live.
Option B (rate): 20% rate reduction on token rates for the first 3 months after go-live, capped at $60,000.

Notes: approvals required — anything > $75k needs Karthik-level signoff per our credit policy. This sits below that threshold but still requires an explicit exec approval memo with an internal rationale and a short MAT (mutual action plan) signoff by Acme.

I can draft the memo and the commercial terms; Laura, can you confirm if we need any contractual language/errata for this kind of remediation? Also need SOW/acceptance criteria tied to the mitigation Marcus is proposing.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Commercial Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Feb 2028 17:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: commercial remediation for delayed multi-model routing support (Acme)

Thanks for the concise options and the product assessment. I reviewed the numbers and the risk profile. Approve Option A (one-time credit of $50,000) with the following conditions:
- Credit is conditional on: Acme signing the attached MAT within 5 business days and committing to the planned pilot acceptance tests.
- Product will ship the 7–10 day config mitigation and provide weekly progress updates until the GA release in May.
- Finance will track usage against the cap and report any overages.

Rishi — please finalize the customer memo and the credit note; Laura, work the contractual language and ensure we have a concise SOW addendum. Tessa, please coordinate the customer comms and get the MAT signed.

I've attached an approval note for the record.

Karthik Iyer
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
attachments: approval-signed.pdf
